name: Amuzgo de Xochistlahuaca, Guerrero
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.

México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano, A.C. xiii+362 pp. (SIL Mexico archive 75518). Corroboration: Apóstol Polanco, Jair. 2024. Dimensiones contrastivas en el núcleo silábico del amuzgo de Xochistlahuaca, Guerrero. Tesis de doctorado, CIESAS, México.
catalog_locator: Buck 2018 §2.4.2 'El acento prosódico', pp. 20-21; also §2.1.2 p. 6 and §2.4.3-2.4.4 pp. 21-23. Apóstol Polanco 2024 §6.3 'Acento y palabra fonológica', pp. 223-225.
catalog_quote: Cada palabra tiene una sílaba que lleva el acento prosódico. Esta sílaba está acentuada, o sea, se pronuncia con una intensidad mayor que las otras sílabas de la palabra. En el amuzgo no se escribe un acento en las palabras. ... En el amuzgo, la sílaba acentuada es generalmente la última sílaba del tema. ... (73) catscu ca.tscu marrano / ta̱nomtyooꞌ ta̱.nom.tyooꞌ papaya / tyotseineiiⁿ tyo.tsei.neiiⁿ estaba hablando / jndyocatseicañeⁿ jndyo.ca.tsei.ca.ñeⁿ vino a avisar. Cuando hay un pronombre dependiente después de la última sílaba del tema de una palabra, esta se acentúa, pero no se escribe un acento. El pronombre no está acentuado; es la sílaba antes del pronombre la que está acentuada: (74) tsotya̱ya tso.tya=ya mi papá / cwilaꞌjndana cwi.laꞌ.jnda=na compran (ellos) ... El tema de muchos verbos y otras palabras termina con el enclítico =ñe animado (véase el capítulo 5), pero como =ñe es un enclítico no lleva el acento; es la sílaba anterior que es la raíz y que lleva el acento prosódico: (75) tyojuꞌñe tyo.juꞌ=ñe brincaba / matsaaⁿñe ma.tsaaⁿ=ñe estornuda ... Cuando los verbos o adjetivos predicativos incluyen un adverbio dependiente ..., el adverbio lleva el acento prosódico. En los siguientes ejemplos, el adverbio dependiente es la última sílaba de la palabra y está escrita en letra negrilla: (76) seijndaxco sei.jnda.xco compró de nuevo / ... tquieeti tquiee.ti es más viejo
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Cada palabra tiene una sílaba que lleva el acento prosódico. Esta sílaba está acentuada, o sea, se pronuncia con una intensidad mayor que las otras sílabas de la palabra. [...] En el amuzgo, la sílaba acentuada es generalmente la última sílaba del tema. [...] Cuando hay un pronombre dependiente después de la última sílaba del tema de una palabra, esta se acentúa, pero no se escribe un acento. El pronombre no está acentuado; es la sílaba antes del pronombre la que está acentuada [...] como =ñe es un enclítico no lleva el acento; es la sílaba anterior que es la raíz y que lleva el acento prosódico [...] Cuando los verbos o adjetivos predicativos incluyen un adverbio dependiente [...], el adverbio lleva el acento prosódico.
new_statements.translation: Every word has one syllable that bears the prosodic stress. This syllable is stressed, i.e. pronounced with greater intensity than the other syllables of the word. [...] In Amuzgo, the stressed syllable is generally the last syllable of the stem. [...] When a dependent pronoun follows the last syllable of the stem of a word, that (stem-final) syllable is stressed, but no accent is written. The pronoun is not stressed; it is the syllable before the pronoun that is stressed [...] since =ñe is an enclitic it does not bear the stress; it is the preceding syllable, which is the root, that bears the prosodic stress [...] When verbs or predicative adjectives include a dependent adverb [...], the adverb bears the prosodic stress.
new_statements.citation: Buck, Marjorie J. 2018. Gramática del amuzgo de Xochistlahuaca, Guerrero. Serie de gramáticas de lenguas indígenas de México 16. México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano, A.C.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (extracted text pp.35-36 = printed pp.20-21). Section 2.4.2 'El acento prosodico' is exactly where stated and every quoted sentence is present verbatim (the [..] gaps skip only the orthography remark 'En el amuzgo no se escribe un acento..' and the example blocks (73)-(76)): 'Cada palabra tiene una silaba que lleva el acento prosodico. Esta silaba esta acentuada, o sea, se pronuncia con una intensidad mayor que las otras silabas de la palabra.. En el amuzgo, la silaba acentuada es generalmente la ultima silaba del tema.' followed by the dependent-pronoun paragraph (tso.tya=ya, cwi.la'.jnda=na), the =ñe enclitic paragraph, and the dependent-adverb paragraph ('el adverbio lleva el acen…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable of the stem (the lexical root, right-aligned; iambic foot). Prefixal/pretonic material is unstressed and reduced; enclitic dependent pronouns and the animate enclitic =ñe are outside the stress domain, so stress is stem-final rather than strictly word-final; dependent (enclitic-like) adverbs, however, do attract the stress to the word-final syllable. Amuzgo is also tonal (3 level tones plus contours) with a ballistic/controlled syllable contrast; these and vowel-length/phonation contrasts are fully realized only in the stressed syllable. Independently confirmed with acoustic data by Apóstol Polanco 2024 ('el acento es fijo y final.. dentro de la raíz', p.223) and by Do Bui 2018 (tonic syllable word-final/right-aligned on the root, p.53, 105); same pattern reported for the Cochoapa variety by de Jesús García 2019 (pp.188-191).
new_statements.secondary_stress: None of the four sources describes a secondary stress; Apóstol Polanco 2024 parses only a single right-aligned iambic foot, leaving initial syllables of trisyllables unfooted.
new_statements.exceptions: Buck: 'generalmente' the last stem syllable; dependent pronouns and enclitic =ñe unstressed, dependent adverbs stressed. Apóstol Polanco 2024 p.225: a single lexical exception with trochaic stress, /tuːja̰/ [ˈtuː²³.ja̰²] 'tapacaminos' (nightjar). Do Bui notes Spanish loans are re-analysed with stress on the right (fn.45, p.72).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the stem/lexical root (tema), not the full clitic group: enclitic pronouns follow the stressed syllable. Tone language; stress is non-contrastive (fixed) per de Jesús García 2019 and Apóstol Polanco 2024. Buck's examples are orthographic citation forms; Apóstol Polanco's measurements are elicited isolated words (3 repetitions, one speaker).
new_statements.identity_note: Buck 2018, Do Bui 2018 and Apóstol Polanco 2024 all describe the Xochistlahuaca variety (Northern/Guerrero Amuzgo, amu = guer1243). de Jesús García 2019 describes the Cochoapa (Guerrero) variety, also classified under amu/guer1243; it independently reports the same final (iambic) stress. Not to be confused with San Pedro Amuzgos Amuzgo (azg, sanp1260), described by Buck 2000, Smith-Stark & Tapia, Herrera Zendejas, Kim.

tone_statements.citation: Herrera Zendejas, Esther. 2014. Patrones fónicos del amuzgo. In Esther Herrera Zendejas, Mapa fónico de las lenguas mexicanas: formas sonoras 1 y 2 (2a ed; 1a ed. 2009 as 'Formas sonoras: mapa fónico de las lenguas mexicanas', Cátedra Jaime Torres Bodet, Estudios de Lingüística 6). México: El Colegio de México. pp. 143-183.
tone_statements.quote: El amuzgo tiene un patrón de seis tonos, tres de ellos son de nivel (A, M, B) y tres de contorno (AB, BM, MA). Los datos siguientes muestran los contrastes. … hndæ (A) polvo hndæ (M) maduro hndæ (B) monte … En los núcleos silábicos con vocales modales, sean orales o nasales, los distintos tonos de nivel se realizan con ligeros deslices a lo largo de toda la vocal; cuando se trata de un tono de contorno, las unidades portadoras incluyen a las nasales, sean éstas segmentos independientes o bien sean parte de la realización de /u) o)/.
tone_statements.translation: Amuzgo has a pattern of six tones, three of them level (H, M, L) and three contour (HL, LM, MH). The following data show the contrasts. … hndæ (H) 'dust' hndæ (M) 'ripe' hndæ (L) 'bush' … In syllable nuclei with modal vowels, oral or nasal, the level tones are realized with slight glides over the whole vowel; with a contour tone, the bearing units include the nasals, whether independent segments or part of the realization of /ũ õ/.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 164-165, section 'Tono: Contrastes tonales' and Tabla 11
tone_statements.summary: Six contrastive tones: three level (high, mid, low) and three contour (high-low, low-mid, mid-high), one per syllable; on breathy/creaky vowels tone sits on the modal part; pitch tracks shown.

tone_statements.citation: Herrera Zendejas, Esther. 2010. En torno a la voz no-modal y la nasalización vocálica en el amuzgo. In Esther Herrera Zendejas (ed.), Entre cuerdas y velo: estudios fonológicos de lenguas otomangues. México: El Colegio de México. pp. 35-64. doi:10.2307/j.ctv6jmx5b.5
tone_statements.quote: El amuzgo tiene un patrón de seis tonos, tres de ellos son de nivel (A, M, B) y tres de contorno (ÁB, BM, MA). Los datos siguientes muestran los contrastes. Tabla5 Contrastes tonales bndre (A) 'polvo' bndre (M) ' maduro' bndre (B) 'monte' … [fn. 3:] la especificación (M, ÁB, :BM) de 'pájaro bobo' indica que la primera sílaba porta un tono medio, la segunda tiene un tono de contorno alto-bajo y la tercera un contorno bajo-medio; cuando una palabra polisilábica tenga una sola melodía tonal, se marcará el tono una vez.
tone_statements.translation: Amuzgo has a pattern of six tones, three of them level (High, Mid, Low) and three contour (High-Low, Low-Mid, Mid-High). The following data show the contrasts. Table 5, Tonal contrasts: hndae (H) 'dust', hndae (M) 'ripe', hndae (L) 'bush' … [fn. 3:] the specification (M, HL, LM) of 'pájaro bobo' indicates that the first syllable carries a mid tone, the second has a high-low contour tone and the third a low-mid contour; when a polysyllabic word has a single tonal melody, the tone is marked once.

tone_statements.citation: Coronado Nazario, Hilario; Ebenecer Coronado Nolasco; Pánfilo de la Cruz Morales; Maurilio Hilario Juárez; Stephen A. Marlett. 2009. Amuzgo del sur (Huixtepec). In Stephen A. Marlett (ed.), Ilustraciones fonéticas de lenguas amerindias. Lima: SIL International y Universidad Ricardo Palma. pp. 2-12 (per Apóstol Polanco 2024).http://lengamer.org/publicaciones/trabajos/amuzgo_huixtepec_afi.pdf
tone_statements.quote: Se presentan tres tonos que pueden llamarse básicos: alto, medio y bajo. … Además se presentan algunas combinaciones de estos tonos, de las cuales aún no se han identificado todas. … La secuencia alto-bajo es especialmente importante. Compare, por ejemplo, estas palabras que se difieren solamente en los tonos: /h a ˥ / ‘nosotros (inclusivo)’, /h a ˧ / ‘yo’, /h a ˩ / ‘amargo’, y /h a ˥ ˩ / ‘nosotros (exclusivo)’. Los tres tonos básicos y el tono contorno alto-bajo se presentan en los siguientes pares mínimos: /t a ˥ / ‘rebanada’, /t a ˧ / ‘grueso’, /t a ˩ / ‘cerro’, /t a ˥ ˩ / ‘papá (voc.)’.
tone_statements.translation: Three tones occur that may be called basic: high, mid and low. ... In addition some combinations of these tones occur, not all of which have yet been identified. ... The high-low sequence is especially important. Compare, for example, these words that differ only in tone: /ha H/ 'we (incl.)', /ha M/ 'I', /ha L/ 'bitter', and /ha HL/ 'we (excl.)'. The three basic tones and the high-low contour tone appear in the following minimal pairs: /ta H/ 'slice', /ta M/ 'thick', /ta L/ 'hill', /ta HL/ 'dad (voc.)'.
tone_statements.locator: p. 6, sec. '3. Tonos' (table and sec. 4 continue on p. 7) (same basename)
tone_statements.summary: Huixtepec (southern) Amuzgo: three basic level tones, high, mid and low, plus combinations such as a high-low contour, shown in minimal sets; a separate final-syllable word stress is proposed.

tone_statements.quote: The following pages show Amy Bauernschmidtꞌs charts of tones for the grammatical persons of possessed nouns of Amuzgo of Xochistlahuaca, Guerrero, Mexico … In the charts the tone given is for the root part of the noun, which is the part before the pronominal suffixes and is the final syllable of stems which have more than one syllable. … (a) A high tone … B A ballistic syllable … (m) A mid tone … C A controlled syllable (b) A low tone (a-b) A high-low tone … (m-a) A mid-high tone … (b-m) A low-mid tone
tone_statements.locator: Buck's 'Explanation of Amy Bauernschmidt's Tone Charts' (footer p. 1) and the tone key under the heading 'CHART OF TONES FOR POSSESSED NOUNS' (footer p. 2 = Buck's 'page 1')
tone_statements.summary: Tone key of six tones (high, mid, low, high-low, mid-high, low-mid) on ballistic or controlled syllables, then paradigm charts of noun-root tone for each possessor person; a key, no prose analysis.

tone_statements.citation: Bauernschmidt, Amy. 2003. Tentative Tone Analysis of Guerrero Amuzgo. Unpublished manuscript, SIL International, Mexico Branch (Bartholomew Collection of Unpublished Materials). SIL Language & Culture Archives item 61493 (OLAC oai:sil.org:61493); file:https://www.sil.org/system/files/reapdata/11/92/65/119265441634238670699973765353841906965/amu_Tone_Analysis.pdf(as consulted by Do Bui 2018, 12-5-2015).
tone_statements.quote: The surface tone patterns are levels: high, mid and low and contours: high-low, mid-high and low-mid. All level and contour tones occur on both ballistic and controlled syllables, except for the LM glide which does not occur on the ballistic syllable. … It appears that level tones H, M and L are basic underlying tones, as well as HL glide. The two rising glides appear to be derived contours due to a floating high. Other tone changes in verb and noun stems may be due to the effects of a floating low tone associated with the ballistic syllable.
tone_statements.locator: Tone pp. 3-4, 'Syllable Types and Tone' (end) and text after the 'Examples of tones' table
tone_statements.summary: Surface tones high, mid, low, high-low, mid-high, low-mid on ballistic and controlled syllables; tentatively H, M, L, HL underlying, rising glides from a floating high; stress on stem-final syllable.

sources.note: §2.4.2 'El acento prosódico' (p.20): every word has one stressed syllable (greater intensity); the stressed syllable is generally the last syllable of the stem (tema); dependent pronouns and the enclitic =ñe are unstressed (stress stays on preceding stem/root syllable); dependent adverbs at word end do take the stress. §2.4.3 ballistic vs controlled syllables, differences most noticeable in stressed syllables; §2.4.4 three tones plus glides.
sources.venue: Serie de gramáticas de lenguas indígenas de México

sources.citation: de Jesús García, Iván. 2019. Fonología del amuzgo de Cochoapa, Guerrero. Tesis de maestría, CIESAS, México. 196 pp.
sources.note: §5.11-5.12 (pp.181-191): in di- and trisyllables prominence falls on the last syllable of the word; Cochoapa Amuzgo has iambic, fixed (Kager 2007) non-contrastive stress: 'El acento en esta lengua cae en la última sílaba'; all phonological contrasts (nasality, phonation, tone) realized in the stressed syllable, reduced in non-prominent syllables.
sources.venue: Tesis de maestría, CIESAS, México. 196 pp

sources.citation: Apóstol Polanco, Jair. 2024. Dimensiones contrastivas en el núcleo silábico del amuzgo de Xochistlahuaca, Guerrero. Tesis de doctorado, CIESAS, Ciudad de México.
sources.note: §6.3 'Acento y palabra fonológica' (pp.220-225): acoustic measurements (duration, F0, intensity) show the second/last syllable of disyllables is prominent; 'el acento es fijo y final en el AX dentro de la raíz'; foot type is iambic; clitics do not shift stress off the last root syllable ('el acento es fijo, porque se mantiene dentro de la última raíz al final de la base'); one lexical exception with a trochee, /tuːja̰/ 'tapacaminos'. §6.4-6.5: full vowel-length, phonation, nasality and tone contrasts only in the tonic (final) syllable; reduced contrasts in atonic syllables.
sources.venue: Tesis de doctorado, CIESAS, Ciudad de México

sources.note: Ch.2 phonology: p.53 'l'accent tonique s'aligne à droite sur la dernière syllabe' and the tonic syllable's 'site est en position finale de mot'; p.105 'L'accent tonique s'aligne à droite sur la racine lexicale ou la syllabe majeure dans une sesquisyllabe'; p.474 'L'accent tonique est iambique sur la racine lexicale'. tone.translation: Three tones occur that may be called basic: high, mid and low. ... In addition some combinations of these tones occur, not all of which have yet been identified. ... The high-low sequence is especially important. Compare, for example, these words that differ only in tone: /ha H/ 'we (incl.)', /ha M/ 'I', /ha L/ 'bitter', and /ha HL/ 'we (excl.)'. The three basic tones and the high-low contour tone appear in the following minimal pairs: /ta H/ 'slice', /ta M/ 'thick', /ta L/ 'hill', /ta HL/ 'dad (voc.)'.

sources.quote: The surface tone patterns are levels: high, mid and low and contours: high-low, mid-high and low-mid. All level and contour tones occur on both ballistic and controlled syllables, except for the LM glide which does not occur on the ballistic syllable. … It appears that level tones H, M and L are basic underlying tones, as well as HL glide. The two rising glides appear to be derived contours due to a floating high. Other tone changes in verb and noun stems may be due to the effects of a floating low tone associated with the ballistic syllable.
